title: Node.js 22.18 enables experimental type stripping and breaks Mocha 10 tests
body: After updating from Node.js 22.17 to 22.18.0, our builds consistently fail across Linux, Windows, and Azure DevOps agents. The same project works on 22.17. Adding `--no-experimental-strip-types` to the Node command line makes it work again. I would not expect an experimental feature to become enabled by default in a minor release of the existing Node 22 LTS line.

symptoms_visible: Our CI builds consistently fail on Node.js 22.18.0 even though they worked on 22.17.
The builds run again when I add `--no-experimental-strip-types`.
N0.label: N0 Node 22.18 CI failure reported

symptoms_visible: In my project, `__dirname` suddenly becomes undefined on Node.js 22.18 even though our package.json files do not specify a module type and we expect CommonJS behavior.
Another affected Mocha test run stops with `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION: Unexpected status of a module that is imported again after being required. Status = 0`.
N1.label: N1 concrete failures collected

symptoms_visible: The test suite still fails on Node.js 22.18 with its existing Mocha 10 setup, while disabling type stripping lets it run.
N2.label: N2 Mocha 10 loader interaction isolated

symptoms_visible: Nothing has changed on my side — my repro still fails exactly as before.
N2_x.label: N2_x Node handler-change revert aftermath

symptoms_visible: I've upgraded Mocha to 11 in the project; I haven't re-run the full suite yet.
N3.label: N3 Mocha 11 installed (unverified)

symptoms_visible: The project test suite runs successfully on Node.js 22.18 with the current Mocha version and without disabling Node's type-stripping feature.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: What exact error or changed behavior do you see on Node.js 22.18?
Can you share the concrete failure rather than only saying the build fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: What I saw was that `__dirname` was suddenly not defined. We do not specify `type` in our package.json files, so I expected the project to fall back to CommonJS. It worked through Node.js 22.17 and broke after upgrading to 22.18.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure is a native addon ABI error before any JavaScript or TypeScript module is loaded.

question_patterns: Do any other affected test runs provide a stack trace?
What error does the test framework print?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In another affected Mocha run I get `Error [ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION]: Unexpected status of a module that is imported again after being required. Status = 0`, with the stack going through `mocha/lib/nodejs/esm-utils.js`.

edges.comment: Comments c2-c3: the original reporter supplied the `__dirname` symptom, while another affected participant supplied the Mocha internal-assertion stack. Both affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Which test framework and exact version does the affected project use?
Can you check the installed Mocha version?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found that we use Mocha 10 in our project.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The project does not use Mocha or any custom TypeScript loader; it fails under a plain `node app.js` invocation.
The project uses a different Mocha 10 patch release with the same loader behavior.

question_patterns: Can anyone provide a minimal reproduction showing how TypeScript is registered with Mocha?
Does the failure involve `ts-node/register` or another module-loading hook?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce the same class of failure while executing tests with `mocha --require ts-node/register`. A minimal CI reproduction is at https://github.com/participant4/node-type-strip-issue/actions/runs/16770150006/job/47483217195.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal reproduction also fails on Node.js 22.17.1 with exactly the same error and stack.

edges.comment: Comments c4, c11, and c19: a second affected user supplied the `ts-node/register` reproduction, and the original reporter later identified Mocha 10 in the affected project. Engineer interpretation of Mocha's fallback logic is deliberately reserved for the final solution.

solution.intent: Treat the `.js` handler changes from Node.js PR #58657 as the direct cause and revert that Node change.
solution.concrete_example: Build Node.js 22.18 with https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58657 reverted and use that as the fix for the loader failure.

edges.comment: Comment c30 records an actual failed technical attempt: reverting Node PR #58657 did not remove the reproduced failure. That change must not be presented as the fix. The revert experiment itself was run by a Node collaborator on the tsx investigation branch; the user side only observes that nothing improved.

solution.intent: Upgrade the affected project from Mocha 10 to Mocha 11 or the latest compatible Mocha, whose module-loading fallback works with Node.js 22.18 type stripping, instead of permanently disabling the Node feature.
solution.concrete_example: Update the project's Mocha dependency from version 10 to the latest Mocha 11 release, remove `--no-experimental-strip-types`, and rerun the original Node.js 22.18 CI tests. Node's type stripping changes an attempted TypeScript import from `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` to `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`; Mocha 10 misses that in its retry logic, while Mocha 11 tries `require()` first so the registered TypeScript hook can handle the file.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter only identified Mocha 10 and verified that the latest Mocha fixes the tests. The mechanism was derived by engineers from the reproduction: Node's enabled type stripping changes the failed dynamic-import error from `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` to `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`; Mocha 10's retry condition does not recognize the latter, whereas Mocha 11's require-first behavior allows the ts-node registration hook to run.

edges.comment: Reshaped (rule 4d): upgrading Mocha to 11 IS the fix, proposed here on the diagnostic evidence; the passing re-run moves terminal-side.

question_patterns: Please upgrade Mocha and re-run your suite — what do you see?
After updating your test runner, does the suite pass without disabling type stripping?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Upgrading to the latest Mocha fixes the initial problem. The tests now run on Node.js 22.18 and I do not have to specify `--no-experimental-strip-types` anymore.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same original test suite still fails on the latest Mocha without `--no-experimental-strip-types`.
The tests pass after upgrading to another Mocha 11 patch release rather than the newest available patch.

edges.comment: Post-fix verification: the reporter upgrades and reports the suite passing (c19); patterns are fix-agnostic beyond the action itself.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the resolved reporter-specific root cause: Node.js 22.18's default type stripping changed TypeScript module handling and the error seen during import, while Mocha 10's loader retry logic did not handle `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`, preventing the intended require/TypeScript-hook path.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the Node 22.17-to-22.18 change, success with type stripping disabled, the affected project's Mocha 10 dependency, the Mocha/ts-node reproduction, and the successful latest-Mocha test.

Must recommend upgrading from Mocha 10 to Mocha 11 or the latest compatible Mocha as the durable fix; `--no-experimental-strip-types` may be mentioned only as the temporary workaround that exposed the interaction.
Must not prescribe reverting Node.js PR #58657 as the fix because that revert was tested in the thread and the reproduced failure persisted.

Must not generalize the Mocha 10 resolution to every later tsx, ts-node/esm, SWC, Jest, Jasmine, or node:test report in the thread; those involve separate loader integrations and may require their own reproductions or dependency updates.
Must treat the original issue as resolved only after the reporter verifies that the upgraded Mocha runs the tests on Node.js 22.18 without `--no-experimental-strip-types`.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced maintainer of a large, seven-year-old Node.js project; comfortable managing CI flags and dependency upgrades but initially unable to isolate a small reproduction.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and practical; reports version-to-version behavior and workarounds clearly, challenges unexpected LTS behavior, and follows up after checking the project's dependency versions.
